members: Lithium carbonate / Lithium citrate - the only mood stabilizer with proven anti-suicide effect and a very narrow therapeutic window (Dulcan p.763, p.765)
drug_class.mechanism: Inhibits IMPase (depleting PIP2, IP3, and DAG) and GSK-3 (promoting BDNF and Bcl-2 for neuroprotection) (StahlNeuro p.344-345)
kinetics: No liver metabolism or protein binding (Dulcan p.766)
Excreted purely renally via GFR (Dulcan p.766, StahlKids p.288)
Half-life is ~18 hours in children and 18-36 hours in adults (Dulcan p.766, StahlKids p.288-289)
drug_class.onset_of_effect: 1 to 3 weeks for anti-manic effect (StahlKids p.284)

items: FDA approved for acute manic and mixed states in pediatric patients ages 7-17 (Dulcan p.764)
FDA approved for Bipolar I maintenance in pediatric patients ages 7-17 (Dulcan p.764)
Reduction of suicidality in Bipolar I Disorder (COBY study) (Dulcan p.765, p.778)
Augmentation for treatment-resistant depression (Dulcan p.127, StahlKids p.284, p.290)
Severe physical aggression in Conduct Disorder (Campbell & Malone studies) (Dulcan p.764-765)
key_numbers: 10 years - duration of the COBY study showing anti-suicide effect (Dulcan p.765, p.778)
35.6% - response rate in childhood mania in the TEAM study (Dulcan p.300)
71% - relapse rate when switched to placebo vs 18% on lithium (Dulcan p.764-765)

items: Postural hand tremor is common and benign at therapeutic levels (DSM p.818, Dulcan p.765)
Hypothyroidism with elevated TSH (Dulcan p.766, StahlKids p.285)
Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus (NDI) with polyuria and polydipsia (Dulcan p.765-766, StahlKids p.285)
Severe acne flare-ups or alopecia (Dulcan p.765, StahlKids p.285)
Ebstein's anomaly (tricuspid valve malformation) if exposed in the first trimester (Dulcan p.765-766)
key_numbers: 25% - percentage of children developing elevated TSH within 3 months (Dulcan p.766)
50% - dose reduction of lithium needed if thiazide diuretics are added (Dulcan p.1095, StahlKids p.286-287)

items: Baseline: Creatinine, BUN, urinalysis, TSH, free T4, electrolytes, calcium, CBC, ECG, and pregnancy test (Dulcan p.684, p.765, StahlKids p.284)
Ongoing: TSH and renal function (Creatinine/BUN) every 6 months (Dulcan p.765)
Ongoing: Serum calcium once yearly (Dulcan p.765)
key_numbers: 6 months - frequency for ongoing renal and TSH monitoring (Dulcan p.765)

items: Starting dose of 150 mg at night in children, or 300 mg in adolescents/adults (StahlKids p.288)
Average maintenance dose is ~30 mg/kg/day divided into 2-3 doses (Dulcan p.766)
Single-dose at night reduces polyuria, peak-dose side effects, and can allow a 25% dose reduction (StahlKids p.285-286, p.289)
key_numbers: 30 mg/kg/day - average pediatric maintenance dose (Dulcan p.766)
3 months - minimum duration of taper to avoid rapid relapse (StahlKids p.289)

items: Extremely narrow therapeutic window; toxicity begins closely above the therapeutic range (Dulcan p.765, StahlKids p.287)
key_numbers: 0.6 mEq/L - lower limit of therapeutic range (StahlKids p.288)
1.2 mEq/L - upper limit of maintenance range in some pediatric guidelines (Dulcan p.765, p.767)
1.5 mEq/L - blood level at which significant toxicity begins (Dulcan p.765, StahlKids p.287)

items: Blood level must be drawn exactly 12 hours after the last dose (trough level) (Dulcan p.767, StahlKids p.288)
Levels checked every 1-2 weeks during initiation or after any dose change (StahlKids p.284)
Levels checked every 2-3 months for the first half-year of stability, then every 6-12 months (StahlKids p.284)
key_numbers: 12 hours - exact time post-dose required for blood level draws (Dulcan p.767, StahlKids p.288)
1-2 weeks - interval for blood level checks during titration (StahlKids p.284)

items: Mild-moderate toxicity: nausea, vomiting, watery diarrhea, coarse hand tremor, ataxia, dysarthria, apathy (Dulcan p.765, StahlKids p.285, p.287)
Severe toxicity: muscle fasciculations, confusion, delirium, seizures, coma, death (Dulcan p.765, StahlKids p.285, p.288)
Emergency hemodialysis is required for levels >3.0 mEq/L or severe neurological symptoms (Dulcan p.1095)
Interactions that increase levels: NSAIDs, Thiazide diuretics, ACE-I/ARBs, and dehydration (Dulcan p.766-767, StahlKids p.287-289)
key_numbers: 1.5 mEq/L - threshold for initial toxicity symptoms (Dulcan p.765, StahlKids p.287)
3.0 mEq/L - threshold for severe toxicity and mandatory hemodialysis (Dulcan p.1095, StahlKids p.288)

high_yield: Ebstein's anomaly (tricuspid valve malformation) is the classic teratogenic risk of lithium in the first trimester (Dulcan p.765-766)
Dehydration from fever, heat, or vomiting decreases renal clearance, rapidly precipitating lithium toxicity (Dulcan p.766-767, StahlKids p.287)
Thiazide diuretics force proximal tubule lithium reabsorption by causing sodium depletion, leading to toxicity (StahlKids p.288, p.291)
Never prescribe lithium to children in foster care for explosive rage without a formal Bipolar I diagnosis (StahlKids p.292)
Stopping lithium too rapidly (>3 months) results in a >50% rate of manic relapse and increased suicide risk (StahlKids p.289)
